unknowns.what: slot names (the `FName` next to each slot's material)
unknowns.why: the cooked slot element is a single 4-byte object reference - there is no name field in the mesh payload, so a slot is identified by its material object; `MATERIALS.md`'s slot numbering is the same object order, not a second field

unknowns.what: the mesh geometry behind the 20 MB of bulk data (vertex counts, bones, bounds per LOD)
unknowns.why: this card decodes the mesh's property tags, slots, sockets and collision; the bulk vertex/index blocks are not decoded here - they are named by `MESHES.md` from an umodel export, which is a different read

unknowns.what: the 662 bytes that differ after the tag stream between Standard's and Playable's `Batmobile_V2`
unknowns.why: the two meshes differ in 1345 bytes in total; the decoded tag layouts are identical, all 19 decoded object-reference fields resolve to the same names, and 2 of the 363 clusters left over have a 4-byte reading whose two values resolve to the same object name. The rest are in the payload's bulk data, where no field is decoded: telling them apart would need the vertex/index/section layout, which this card does not decode (`MESHES.md`'s geometry comes from an umodel export, a different read)

unknowns.what: which skin the drivable car selects, and when
unknowns.why: the packages hold four meshes; the code that swaps `Batmobile_V2` for `Batmobile_MK2_Skin` / `Batmobile_Jokerfied_Skin` is not in them - it would be a class default or a Kismet action (G3-02/G3-06)

unknowns.what: the material-parameter effect on screen (whether any decoded difference is visible)
unknowns.why: the parameters are decoded, the shader that consumes them is not; see `COLOUR.md` for what is missing between a parameter and a pixel
